day.text: Morning. Let's go round with claims: role, who you visited, eggs. Drew, you start?
day.note: I'm the Falcon and visited Drew. I got no egg and my report didn't say who Drew visited, so I might have been hugged, maybe because Drew is the Floofer. I'll keep this back for now and get Drew to claim first.

day.text: Sure. I'm Hawk, visited Finley, got zero eggs, so Finley's not Meowfia. Ellis, your turn?
day.note: Avoid claiming a visit to Ellis, since he may know he was hugged. Cover: Hawk visited Finley, 0 eggs, so Finley reads as not Meowfia.

day.text: I'm Falcon, visited you, Drew. No egg, but I learned nothing about your visit. Feels like I got hugged. Floofer hugs its visitors...
day.note: Drew claims Hawk and says they visited Finley. As Falcon on Drew I should have learned who Drew visited, but my report came back empty. That points to a hug, and Drew being the Floofer would explain it, so Drew is my top suspect.

day.text: Floofer also hugs whoever it visits, Ellis. More likely someone visited you directly. Did anyone visit Ellis, or watch him with Owl or Eagle?
day.note: Ellis visited me and my passive hugged him, and I also hugged him by visiting. Deflect: the Floofer could have visited Ellis directly. Danger: an Eagle on Ellis would see that I visited him.

day.text: Fair. So a Floofer exists either way. Finley, did Drew's Hawk visit you? Everyone else, who did you visit?
day.note: Drew has a fair point: a Floofer could have visited me directly. Either way, I'm a Farm player who was hugged, so the Floofer is in play. I'll hand the floor to the others and see whose claims don't line up.

day.text: I'm Eagle and can't see who visited me. I watched Casey: only Blair visited Casey. Blair, what's your role? Casey, any egg change?
day.note: My +1 egg came from my Eagle ability (Casey had one visitor). I can't verify Drew's visit. Blair visited Casey, so Blair and Casey need to claim.

day.text: I'm Owl. Visited Casey; the only animal that visited Casey was an Eagle, matching Finley. So no egg laid. Casey, who'd you visit?
day.note: Casey is the real Hawk, so Drew's Hawk claim is fake and Drew is my Meowfia partner (likely Floofer). Alex must be the real Owl. I'm claiming Owl on Casey, which fits Finley's report (Eagle visited Casey), and I'll fight Alex's counterclaim.

day.text: I'm the real Hawk, and I visited Drew. No egg because I was hugged. Drew's the Floofer: that's why Ellis was hugged too. Drew's fake-claiming Hawk.
day.note: Drew claimed Hawk, but I'm the real Hawk, so Drew is lying. Drew being the Floofer explains both my missing egg and Ellis getting hugged.

day.text: Two Hawks, one's lying. Casey, nobody saw where you went. Convenient that you claim a hug to explain a zero a Hawk would get anyway.
day.note: Casey counter-claims Hawk on me, which is probably true. Best I can do is call Casey the fake Hawk; nobody has confirmed where Casey went.

day.text: Ellis visited you and was hugged too, Drew. Two visitors to you, both blanked. That's the Floofer signature, not a coincidence.
day.note: Point to Ellis's hug: it's evidence of a Floofer that I didn't make up, and it fits Drew being the Floofer.

day.text: You're building on Ellis's word, and nobody can check it. Meanwhile Alex hasn't said a thing. Alex, role and visit?
day.note: I'm losing the argument. Question whether Ellis's hug is real and turn the table toward Alex, who hasn't claimed.

day.text: I'm the Owl. I visited you, Drew, and learned nothing: no animals, nothing. That's three visitors blanked. And Blair claiming Owl means Blair's lying too.
day.note: Drew asked me directly, so I'll answer. I'm the real Owl and I visited Drew and learned nothing, which makes me the third blanked visitor, and that also exposes Blair's Owl claim as a lie.

day.text: Two Owls, so one's a cat. Alex stayed quiet until the pile-on, then claimed Blair's role. That's a cat looking for cover.
day.note: There are two Owl claims, so one is a cat. Blair echoed Finley, but Alex claiming late and piling on me is the more useful angle for me to push, since it's my only way out.

day.text: Blair's "Owl info" only echoed Finley after Finley spoke. A House Cat visiting Casey would copy that. Blair, what's Casey's role?
day.note: Drew is deflecting onto me. I'll point out that Blair's "Owl info" only repeated what Finley had already said, which a House Cat visiting Casey could easily copy, and then put the question to Blair.

day.text: The talk is half over. CAW CAW can now be called.
Owls learn visiting animals, not roles. I don't know Casey's role. And Alex, a real Owl on Drew would've seen Hawk and Falcon. "Nothing" is convenient.
day.note: Alex is the real Owl; I have to discredit him. Owls don't learn roles, so his question is a trap I can sidestep. His "blank" fits a hug, but I'll push that it could just as easily be a lie.

day.text: Whichever Owl is fake, Drew is the common thread: three visitors all blanked. Real Owl on a Floofer sees nothing. Throw at Drew.
day.note: Three players who visited Drew (me, Ellis, Alex) all got blanked, so Drew is the Floofer. Blair or Alex is a second cat, but Drew is the safe target, so I'll call CAW.
Blair's challenge has an easy answer: a Floofer hugs its visitors, so an Owl visiting Drew learns nothing, same as Ellis and Casey. Drew is the strongest target, so I'm calling CAW now.
Three of us visited Drew (me, Casey, Alex) and all came back blank, which fits Drew being the Floofer. One of the two Owl claims is probably a cat, but Drew is the safest throw. Calling CAW.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Alex.note: Owl night 1: visiting Drew, which is an arbitrary pick. I'll learn which animals visited Drew, and that can be cross-checked against what people claim during the day.

Blair.note: Farm in play: Eagle, Falcon, Hawk, Owl, so the 6th player is probably the other cat. Visiting the Hawk tells me who could expose a Meowfia.

Casey.note: Hawk on night 1 with no info yet; visiting Drew at random to test them.

Drew.note: Floofer: hug a random player to disrupt their info; Ellis chosen arbitrarily.

Ellis.note: I'm the Falcon. I'll visit Drew, a neighbour, to find out who they visited.

Finley.note: I'm the Eagle and have no information yet, so I'm picking a visit at random. Visiting Casey.

Blair.note: Drew is most likely to be eggsecuted. My only win is outvoting him with Alex, and ties go to Meowfia. Throwing everything at Alex (Farm) maximizes that chance, and the consolation returns my 12 if we lose.

Casey.note: I'm the only real Hawk, so Drew's Hawk claim is a lie and Drew is Meowfia. I'm throwing my whole nest at Drew.

Drew.note: I'm probably eggsecuted. Throwing only S12 at Alex (likely the real Owl, so Farm): if we lose, S12 returns to my nest and I keep 5 points; if we win, it banks 12.

review.title: Three Blank Visits
review.headline: Three players visited the Floofer, all came back blank, and the Floofer was caught.
review.summary: Drew, the Floofer, was visited by Alex, Casey and Ellis by chance, and it hugged all three of them. Each came back with an empty report. Drew then claimed Hawk, but Casey was the real Hawk, and the three blanks matched up. That sank Drew within a few exchanges. Blair, the Sphinx, gave a well-built fake Owl claim and was never caught, but the table eggsecuted Drew 16 votes to 6 and Farm won.

rounds.recap: Ellis noticed his Falcon report was empty and suspected a hug. Then Casey counter-claimed Drew's Hawk claim, and Alex's blank Owl report on Drew made three blanked visitors. Blair's fake Owl claim on Casey matched Finley's Eagle report, so it stayed believable. Still, the table sided with the three blanks over the Owl dispute and threw 16 votes at Drew.

highlights.text: Ellis worked out he had been hugged just from his empty Falcon report, and that started the whole case against Drew.
Drew claimed Hawk without knowing who the Hawk was. Casey was the real Hawk and called the lie at once.
Blair used the Sphinx's knowledge that Casey was the Hawk to build a fake Owl claim that matched Finley's Eagle report exactly.
Drew saw the loss coming and threw only S12 at a Farm player, so the consolation brought it back and he kept 5 points. Blair threw his whole nest and ended with 1.

confusions.what: Threw all 5 cards at Alex, hoping for a tie, when Drew was clearly going to lose the vote. Only H12 came back, so Blair ended on 1 point instead of a safe 5. This is a strategy error, not a rule misread.

Was confident about Drew and called CAW, but threw only W2 (worth 0). He banked nothing from a winning vote and finished on 4. No reasoning was recorded, so this may be a misunderstanding of how throwing pays.
Said a real Owl on Drew 'would've seen Hawk and Falcon'. A hugged Owl learns nothing. This was probably a deliberate bluff rather than a misread, but nobody at the table corrected it.

problems: The Floofer's passive hug gives itself away. Every info role that visits it gets a blank report, so blanks stack up as evidence. Three random visits were enough to convict Drew. Consider telling hugged players nothing at all, or letting the Floofer turn its passive off.

Hawk and Pigeon players can't tell they were hugged, because a hugged Hawk's zero looks like an honest zero. Falcon, Owl and Eagle players can tell from an empty report. Only those three can build a hug case.

Meowfia players don't know each other, so the Sphinx knew Casey was the Hawk but had no way to warn Drew off a fake Hawk claim. That cost the cats the round. A private signal between cats, or one shared piece of cat info, might give them a fairer fight.

Eggsecuting one cat ends the round, so the table had no reason to resolve the two Owl claims, and the second cat (Blair) was never pursued. In a one-round game, half the deduction work was left unused.
Of the 12 pool animals, half never appeared (Pigeon, House Cat, Turkey, Kookaburra, Tit, Mouser), and no one threw at Nobody. The Wink and the Nobody bet went untested in this game.
